patch_resolves_note: The fixed OpenThread build keeps the original 200-bit Prefix TLV case clean by rejecting it before storage, and the adjacent 128-bit aligned boundary case still reaches both `stored_prefix` and `prefix_copy_sink` on vulnerable and fixed builds, providing a genuine fixed-side witness for the repaired path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First direct project-side consumption of the attacker-controlled Thread Network Data TLV payload on the vulnerability path. Leader registration starts parsing the raw network-data byte span that came from the received Server Data message.

Executed admission check that lets the malformed Prefix TLV survive registration. In the vulnerable commit, `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` only checks TLV-internal length consistency and does not require `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)`, so an oversized prefix length still passes validation.

ASan sink. `GetNextOnMeshPrefix` copies `BitVectorBytes(prefix->GetPrefixLength())` bytes from the stored malformed Prefix TLV into the stack-local `otBorderRouterConfig config`, but the destination field `mPrefix.mPrefix` is only a 16-byte IPv6 address.
Intermediate runtime event stored_prefix materialized from verified transition assertion A-PREFIX-BYTES-PERSIST-TO-STORED-PREFIX.

edges.description: The oversized byte span derived from the incoming Prefix TLV at the missing-bound admission gate is copied unchanged into the newly stored leader Prefix TLV.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records prefix_bound_check.prefix_bytes == stored_prefix.stored_prefix_bytes == 25.

edges.description: The same stored prefix byte span is re-read from leader network data and used as the memcpy length at the later `GetNextOnMeshPrefix` sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records stored_prefix.stored_prefix_bytes == prefix_copy_sink.copy_bytes == 25.
